subject: Re: ScopeMetrics - volume pricing, model premiums, and next steps
messages:
From: Kiran Shah <kiran@scopemetrics.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@scopemetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Volume / model pricing — initial details

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. A few follow-ups from our side so we can move pricing into procurement: 

- We currently expect ~1.2B tokens/month of mixed traffic (search snippets + chat assist). Peak concurrency will be modest but steady.
- We want to understand how Redwood thinks about blended pricing across model families (standard vs premium GPUs/architectures) and embeddings vs chat.
- Do you have a clean annual commitment slab that maps to per-token discounts? Also curious about how model-level premiums (e.g., premium-chat vs standard-chat) are expressed — flat multiplier vs per-token delta?

I've attached a run rate export for three months so you can see the mix. Procurement will want an initial number to evaluate budget impact. Can you share a proposal that includes:
  * 1-year vs 3-year commit options
  * explicit per-token rates by tier and model class
  * how embeddings are priced (per 1k tokens or per-call)
  * any minimum spend or ramp schedule

Appreciate it — Kiran

Attachments: ScopeMetrics_Usage_RunRate_202703.xlsx
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Kiran Shah <kiran@scopemetrics.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@scopemetrics.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Volume / model pricing — initial details

Hi Kiran — great to meet you and thanks for the usage sample. High-level proposal below; I'll follow up with a formal quote and a simple Excel that maps your run-rate to per-month payment.

Proposal (hosted API, per-token billing, USD):
- No-commit (on-demand): standard model baseline $0.00060 / token; premium-chat model baseline $0.00180 / token; embeddings $0.00020 / token (per token output + input).
- 1-year commit slabs (monthly charge is derived from annual committed spend):
  * Bronze: 25M tokens/mo => 10% off baseline per-token rates
  * Silver: 250M tokens/mo => 25% off baseline per-token rates
  * Gold: 1.5B tokens/mo => 40% off baseline per-token rates
- Model premium handling: we apply a model multiplier to the committed blended rate rather than a fixed absolute surcharge. Example: premium-chat = 3.0x standard, embeddings are priced independently at the discounted embedding rate.
- Ramp & true-ups: first 3 months are treated as ramp (no penalty if below committed level), months 4–12 we reconcile actuals vs commit with true-ups billed monthly.
- For customers requiring deeper discounts ( >2B tokens/mo committed), we can move to custom blended SKUs and/or provide a dedicated capacity conversation (Dedicated offering).

Pros: simple math for procurement, consistent multipliers for model families. Cons: if your mix is heavily premium-chat, the multiplier model can look higher than per-model deltas — we can provide a blended example in the spreadsheet.

I'll attach an initial costing sheet that shows your run rate mapped to Bronze/Silver/Gold. If this aligns, I'll generate an official quote and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: price_model_costing_v1.csv
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Kiran Shah <kiran@scopemetrics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Volume / model pricing — initial details

Looping in internal pricing thoughts — one operational note for procurement: if we move to a per-model absolute delta (instead of multiplier), it simplifies their forecasting because they can partition traffic by model and compute spend deterministically. Multipliers are conceptually simpler for us but harder for customers with diverse model mixes.

Two options to present in the quote:
1) Multiplier approach (as Aisha outlined): fewer SKUs and easier to roll out — good for customers expecting stable mix.
2) Per-model delta (explicit per-token surcharge for named premium models): more SKUs but clearer per-call cost for engineering/finops teams.

Also — we should confirm whether procurement needs the SLA revenue credit terms spelled out in the quote (Laura?), and whether the MSLA draft needs the reserved-capacity opt-out language removed for hosted-only deals.

—Marissa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: margin and approval constraints for ScopeMetrics

Internal note (not for external):
- Target gross margin floor for hosted deals at this scale: ~55–65% depending on model mix. Premium models reduce margin materially.
- Approvals: any headline discount >35% requires VP approval; >50% requires CFO review.
- Suggested path for this opportunity: offer a Silver slab (25% off baseline) for year-1 with an option to reprice at year-2 based on actual premium model usage. Provide a short-term pilot addendum (90 days) at an extra nominal discount to accelerate signature.

Attached a quick cost model that derives break-even token price at different mixes. If Aisha wants, I can produce a blended quote that shows both multiplier and absolute-delta views side-by-side for procurement.

Attachments: SCOPE-MSLA-draft-v2.pdf

Regards,
Rishi
From: Kiran Shah <kiran@scopemetrics.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@scopemetrics.com, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@scopemetrics.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Volume / model pricing — initial details

Aisha / Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown and the options. Quick answers from procurement:
- They prefer explicit per-model deltas (procurement + engineering want deterministic per-call costing).
- They want a 1-year commit but with a 90-day pilot clause and monthly true-ups as you suggested.
- Target: finalize in April; procurement needs an official quote + MSLA for legal review and DocuSign routing.

Can you send a formal quote that shows: Bronze/Silver/Gold slabs with absolute per-token rates for standard-chat, premium-chat (named model examples), and embeddings; include the 90-day pilot addendum and the SLA credit language. If possible, include a sample monthly invoice that shows how true-ups will appear.

If you can get that over by EOD Thursday (2027-04-01), procurement will prioritize review and we can schedule a signature call.

Thanks — Kiran
